title: US Army OCS 2026: Requirements, Age & Training
metaDescription: US Army OCS 2026: bachelor's degree, US citizenship, age 19-32, GT score 110, secret clearance, then 12 weeks at Fort Benning and commissioning.
headline: US Army Officer Candidate School 2026: Requirements & Training

sections.title: What OCS is and who it is for
sections.content:
Officer Candidate School at Fort Benning, Georgia is the US Army's main commissioning path for people who already hold a bachelor's degree and want to become officers without going through ROTC or West Point. It is also the route for prior-enlisted soldiers who earn a degree and seek a commission.

Civilians attend Basic Combat Training first, a 10-week course, before starting OCS, while enlisted candidates arrive through their chain of command. Roughly two-thirds of applicants are accepted, so preparation, fitness and a clean record matter as much as the degree itself.

sections.title: Eligibility: degree, age, citizenship and scores
sections.content:
The hard requirements are a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution in any major, US citizenship with no waivers, and eligibility for a secret security clearance. The commonly cited age range is 19 to 32, though official accession rules set the board-age ceiling near the 40th birthday with waivers, so candidates near the edges should confirm the current rule with a recruiter.

Candidates also need a GT score of 110 or higher on the ASVAB with no waivers, must meet height and weight standards, and must pass the Army Fitness Test standards. Enlisted applicants must have fewer than six years of Active Federal Service on arrival at OCS, and moral waivers for past offences are handled case by case.

sections.title: The 12-week course: three phases to commission
sections.content:
OCS runs 12 weeks in three phases. Phase I covers foundational officership, Army customs, physical fitness and land navigation; Phase II adds tactical leadership, decision-making under stress and peer leadership evaluations; Phase III culminates in a field training exercise where candidates perform as platoon leaders in evaluated scenarios.

Candidates who fall short of a standard may be recycled into a later class or dismissed, and attrition is real, though most committed candidates who arrive fit complete the course. Graduates commission as second lieutenants and move on to branch-specific Basic Officer Leader Course training, which lasts from about 8 to 52 weeks depending on branch.

sections.title: Branches, pay and life after OCS
sections.content:
OCS graduates are assigned across branches including Infantry, Armor, Field Artillery, Signal, Engineers, Military Intelligence, Medical Services Corps, Transportation, Quartermaster, Finance, Military Police, Ordnance, Adjutant General and Air Defense Artillery. Branch assignment reflects performance, preferences and Army needs.

New second lieutenants earn officer base pay plus housing and subsistence allowances, with the standard three-year active duty service obligation after commissioning. The career path then runs through platoon leadership, company-grade staff roles and captain's career courses, making OCS one of the fastest routes from civilian graduate to Army officer.

faqs.q: What degree do you need for Army OCS?
faqs.a: You need a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution, in any major, by the time you commission. Enlisted soldiers still in college can enter OCS before finishing, but must complete the degree within a year of enrolment. STEM degrees are viewed favourably, though the Army accepts all accredited majors for OCS applicants.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for Army OCS?
faqs.a: The commonly cited range is 19 to 32 years, with Reserve applicants sometimes cited from 18. Official accession rules set a higher board-age ceiling near the 40th birthday, with waivers for older applicants in some circumstances, so anyone near a boundary should confirm the current rule with a recruiter before applying.

faqs.q: Do you need to be a US citizen for OCS?
faqs.a: Yes, all OCS applicants must be US citizens, with no waivers on citizenship. You must also be eligible for a secret security clearance, which involves character screening covering finances, drug and alcohol history, foreign ties and criminal record, so disclose everything early rather than letting the investigation surface it.

faqs.q: How long is Army OCS and what happens after?
faqs.a: OCS is a 12-week course at Fort Benning in three phases: basic officership and fitness, intermediate tactical leadership, and an advanced field exercise as platoon leader. After commissioning as a second lieutenant, officers attend branch-specific Basic Officer Leader Course training lasting roughly 8 to 52 weeks, then serve a three-year active duty obligation.

Yes, prior-enlisted soldiers are a large share of OCS classes. They need a bachelor's degree, fewer than six years of Active Federal Service on arrival, a GT score of 110 or higher, and a record that supports a commission. Their experience is an advantage in peer leadership evaluations, though they complete the same 12-week course as civilians.
